observation.visible_scene: A dance studio with a floor-to-ceiling mirror wall along the left, a draped sage-green curtain on the right wall (also seen reflected in the mirror), a ballet barre and potted plants along the mirror, light stands, a pale wood floor and a dark ceiling with light panels. A woman with long dark hair, an olive tank top and black flared pants, barefoot, stands with her back partly to the camera facing the mirror; her front-facing reflection is visible in the mirror. The clip is a temporally cropped excerpt, so the action is already in progress at the start and unfinished at the end.
visible_changes: At the start the dancer's right arm is extended outward toward the mirror and then progressively raised overhead while her legs are spread wide, weight on one leg.
She bends her knees and lowers her torso, bringing her right hand up beside her head with the elbow out; her hair swings as her body turns, indicating a rotation of the upper body/head.
The right arm is raised overhead again, then returns to the head, repeating this arm path several times while the knees stay bent.
She then lifts and bends her left leg behind her, and transitions into a pose with the left leg extended back (toe pointed) and both arms bent forward at chest height.
For the final stretch of frames she holds that extended-leg, arms-forward position with only small adjustments, while the reflection tracks all of these movements.

The overall framing of the dancer within the shot shifts slightly across the clip (the dancer appears more central and smaller toward the end), but it is not clear whether this is camera reframing or the dancer's own translation.
outside_clip_unknowns: What movement preceded the initial extended-arm pose at t=0.
What the held end pose develops into after the excerpt ends.
Whether the apparent change in framing is a camera move or the dancer shifting position in the room.
uncertain_details: Cause of the slight change in shot framing (camera pan/zoom vs. dancer translation) is not determinable from the background evidence.
Exact dance terminology of the poses is not specified; only the visible arm/leg/body configuration is described.
